case_name: Hitesh Verma v. State of Uttarakhand and Another

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
Criminal Appeal No. 707 of 2020
Hitesh Verma ... Appellant
versus
State of Uttarakhand and Another ... Respondents
Coram: L. Nageswara Rao, Hemant Gupta and Ajay Rastogi, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 05 November, 2020

HEMANT GUPTA, J.:
1. The challenge in the present appeal is to an order passed by the High Court of Uttarakhand dismissing an application filed by the appellant under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for quashing of the charge-sheet and summoning order in respect of offences punishable under Sections 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

11. The basic ingredients of an offence under Section 504 IPC are that there must be an intentional insult and it must give provocation to any person intending or knowing that it is likely to break the public peace. In the absence of any allegation of public view, the offence cannot be sustained.

18. The inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is intended to prevent the abuse of the process of any court and to secure the ends of justice. Where the allegations in the FIR and charge-sheet do not disclose the commission of any cognizable offence, continuation of criminal proceedings constitutes harassment.
